title: Bull's Club band contests and Milneburg
summary: Tuesday night multi-band contests at the Elks Hall yards and the many bands at Milneburg pavilions.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh yeah, that's what that was for. And they advertised every Sunday. Oh that was wonderful.
Do you remember any famous contests they had bucking like that?
Well that would go on every Tuesday over and over and over.
Who would you even do when?

Well they never would come to the conclusion. Who would win is just move from one side, in other words when this band play on this side the crowd come over and listen to that band. And when the middle band play they go inside, and the next one they go on the other side. And so it worked like that.
Would they, now let's see, that's the Elks Hall now. That's right, that's right.
Well they had a big yard on each side. See from the Elks place to Daniel Street, all that was the open space. And from that part to dry on that side, then they had the hall in the middle.
And they'd have one band in either yard?
Yeah, one on this side and one on the other side. Sometime one in the middle. Every Tuesday, that was a big night.
Why did they pick Tuesday? That's a funny day of the week.
Well at that time people used to look like, it seems to me, they went for the music more than anything and had this jukebox and so forth. And at Millenburg they had something going on every day.
Oh it was fine. The pavilions, they'd have some time, I imagine about six or seven bands out there.
Who would be out there at once? Do you remember who the different guys would be?
Well all the bands, Rene Band, Punchy was under the name of Kid Punchy at that time, Punchy Band, Chris Band, Jack Kerris Band, Sam Morgan Band. Kidman. All those fellas.
Sweet ones. Must have kept things jumping. Oh yeah.
That was the good old days.
